summary: c1 is introduced: the before source has no reparse deferral mechanism, while the after source requires a later nonfinal parse call that the fixed harness never makes.

claims.necessity_reason: The review established this target-coverage obligation; this turn assesses only when it arose.

before.requirement: Exercise default-enabled reparse deferral after an incomplete-token attempt.
before.reason: The before source calls the processor directly and has no callProcessor definition, so this same deferral behavior did not yet exist.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The before buffer path sets finalBuffer and invokes the processor directly.

after.requirement: Exercise the default-enabled deferral branch through successive nonfinal parse calls on one parser after an incomplete token.
after.reason: The new helper can defer only after an earlier partial-token attempt while finalBuffer is false. Each target parser gets one nonfinal call followed by a final call.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: Each newly created parser starts with zero prior partial-token bytes and deferral enabled by default.
The buffer path sets finalBuffer from isFinal before calling the helper.
The zero-context direct path has the same finalBuffer ordering.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: The entry repeats that two-call sequence on distinct parsers.
The fixed recipe builds this parse fuzzer.

claims.comparison_reason: The innermost blocking condition is the new helper's requirement for a later nonfinal attempt with insufficient added data. That condition did not exist before; the before code invoked the processor directly. The same old harness therefore has an introduced coverage gap for this tuple.
